Subject: URGENT: Decline investigation request — ORBIT-2026-Q1-42 / OVW-2026-03

Hi Stripe Support,

Requesting assistance investigating repeated card declines for our customer OrbitWave (account ORBIT-2026-Q1-42). Details below:

- Invoice: OVW-2026-03
- Amount: $18,750.00
- Payment attempt dates: 2026-03-11 (auto), 2026-03-12 (manual retry)
- Payment_intent id: pi_3Kq7NWbPqXx9aVCe2Yb0L1c2
- Decline code (as reported by customer): do_not_honor

Customer reports issuer returned a 'Do Not Honor' and is investigating. We want to know if Stripe (or acquiring bank) has any additional decline metadata (e.g., risk_score, reason_code, acquirer_response) or if there's an acquirer-level block. Also: is there an elevated risk of a subsequent chargeback if we continue retries?

We’ve attached a screenshot from the customer. Can you:
- Confirm what the decline code translates to on your side and any available acquirer/issuer notes.
- Advise whether a hosted card update link (Stripe customers.update method) is recommended versus retrying.
- Provide estimated time to return any issuer notes so we can communicate to the customer.

Case context: this customer is mid-expansion and we prefer to avoid service interruption. If helpful, we can provide the raw event logs/email addresses.

Attachment: decline_screenshot_Mar12.png

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Subject: Re: URGENT: Decline investigation request — ORBIT-2026-Q1-42 / OVW-2026-03

Hi Karthik — thanks for the details. We've reviewed the payment attempts and opened case CS-8921-OW. Summary:

- Decline code: do_not_honor (issuer responded). Our acquirer did not return additional specific AVS/CAA notes.
- Risk/score: no automated fraud block triggered in our system for these attempts.
- Likely cause: issuer-level decline or card network flag.

Recommendations:
1) Provide OrbitWave with a hosted card update link (Payment Method collection via Checkout or SetupIntent) — that will likely be the fastest path to resolution.
2) Avoid repeated automated retries from your system for the same payment_intent; multiple retries can increase the chance of a block.
3) If OrbitWave reports an unexpected charge or files a dispute, use case CS-8921-OW as a reference and supply any customer communications and the signed TOS if a chargeback occurs.

We can try one additional auth if you prefer, but the success probability is low without issuer interaction. If you want, we can also request issuer notes from the acquirer — ETA 48-72 hours, subject to acquirer policy.

Case link: https://dashboard.stripe.com/support/cases/CS-8921-OW (Stripe login required)

If you confirm you'd like a hosted update link, we can share recommended Checkout/SetupIntent parameters.

Regards,
Stripe Support Team
support@stripe.com
